subject: spaceGalley
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: spaceship galley kitchen.
Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo.

spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: A cutaway diorama of the grimy, lived-in galley and mess of a 1979 commercial tow ship: stainless counter run, locker wall with coffee machine and CRT, a bolted central mess table, a hazard-striped hatch and overhead pipework, all lit amber and green.
spec.layout: A room 3.6 m wide (x ±1.8), 4.2 m long (z -2.1 to +2.1) and 2.6 m tall, open at the front (+Z) and with no solid ceiling, so the interior reads like a film set. It stands on y = 0, and the shell's floor deck is the only part that touches y = 0. Walls stand 0.1 m thick: left wall (+X) inner face x = 1.7, right wall (-X) inner face x = -1.7, back wall inner face z = -2.0 with its outer skin at z = -2.1. The ceiling is an open grid of steel beams at y 2.5 to 2.6. Left wall (+X): the stainless galley counter run, z -1.95 to 1.3, depth x 1.05 to 1.7, top at y 0.95, with overhead cabinets above. Right wall (-X): a tall locker bank with fridge, freezer and dry store at z -1.95 to 0.3, then a coffee/dispenser bench at z 0.3 to 1.35, with a CRT and shelf above it. Back wall: a centred hazard-striped hatch (x ±0.55), control panel and conduit. Centre: a bolted pedestal mess table (x ±0.45, z -0.2 to 1.4, top y 0.78) with a fixed bench on each long side, and cups, trays and rations on it. Over the table hang caged work lamps and a ceiling pipe run. Mood: 1970s industrial, a used-future truck-stop kitchen. Dull cream and grey painted panels, stainless steel, scuffed black rubber, grime darkening every lower edge, rivets and seams on every panel, hand-stencilled labels. Small amber and green lights, CRT glow and caged white lamps are the only colour, and they glow. Everything is chunky boxes, cylinders and plates with visible bolts. Nothing is cute, shiny or clean.

parts.builds:
The room structure only, with nothing mounted on it.
FLOOR: a 3.6 x 4.2 m deck, y 0 to 0.1, built as a deckGrate base slab with a grid of thin raised deckPlate bars forming grating, plus a few larger bolted deckPlate rectangles under the counter and table zones. A hazardYellow/hazardBlack stripe pair runs along the front threshold. Dark grime wedges sit in the corners.
WALLS: three wall slabs (left, right and back) with the inner faces above. Each is a wallCream upper field and a wallGrey lower dado to y 0.9, split into a grid of panels by thin seam strips. Rivet rows (small flat cylinders in steelDark) run along the seams. A darker wallDark skirting runs along the base. Grime streaks (thin grime boxes) run down from the seams and pool at the bottom. Vertical wallDark corner posts stand at the three corners, plus end posts at z 2.0 on the side walls. A few rust patches sit near the floor.
CEILING FRAME: an open grid at y 2.5 to 2.6 of steelDark I-beams, two longitudinal beams along z at x ±1.7 and cross beams every 1.0 m along z, with bolt plates at the crossings. Add yellow-black stencil blocks on two beams.
Keep wall interiors flat enough that other parts can sit on the inner faces.
parts.attaches: Floor top at mount floorTop (y 0.1). Wall inner faces at x ±1.7 and z -2.0 (leftWallFace, rightWallFace, backWallFace). Beam undersides at y 2.5 (ceilingUnderside). All other parts build against these.

parts.builds:
The left-wall stainless galley run, x 1.05 to 1.7, z -1.95 to 1.3, y 0.1 to 2.05.
BASE UNITS: a wallDark toe-kick plinth y 0.1 to 0.2. Above it sit steelDark cabinet boxes with a grid of steel doors and drawers. Each front carries a bar handle, scuffed edges as thin grime strips and 4 corner rivets. Stencilled label plates in enamel.
COUNTERTOP: steel slab at y 0.95 with a raised lip and a steelBright front edge, plus grime stains.
COOKTOP at z about -0.3: four burner rings (dark cylinders with small amber flame-ring glow), a hob plate, four black knobs on the front fascia, an oven below with a door window glowing amber and a handle bar. A dented pot (steelDark cylinder with lid and handles) and a frying pan sit on the burners.
SINK at z about 0.7: a recessed basin (box with a dark interior), a tall neck tap with a lever, a draining board with ribs and a dish rack holding enamel plates.
EXTRACTOR HOOD: a tapered steel hood over the cooktop, y 1.55 to 1.95, with a duct up, a small amber lamp and a grease filter grille.
OVERHEAD CABINETS: y 1.45 to 2.05, x 1.35 to 1.7, two or three boxes with latches, flanking the hood, with hazard-stencil tags.
UTENSIL RAIL: a steel bar on the wall at y 1.2 with hooks, a ladle, whisk and spatula, plus a hanging oven glove in rationOlive. A small wall-mounted timer box with an amber light and a few clips and cups on a shelf.
Colours: steel, steelDark, steelBright, rubber, enamel, grime, amber, alarmRed (one status lamp).
parts.attaches: Back sits against leftWallFace (x 1.7). Base units stand on floorTop. Countertop at counterTop (y 0.95), front at counterFront (x 1.05). Overhead cabinet base at overheadCabinetBase (y 1.45). Nothing above y 2.05.

parts.builds:
The central dining set. Table: x ±0.45, z -0.2 to 1.4, top at y 0.78.
TABLE: a thick steel top slab (steelDark with steelBright rim band and rubber edge trim) on a squat central pedestal (a chunky octagonal or box column) with a wide base plate bolted to the deck (rivets and a grime ring), plus two cross braces. The top has inset recessed tray lanes (darker plates) and bolted-on condiment clips.
BENCHES: two fixed benches, x ±(0.52 to 0.80), z 0 to 1.2, top at y 0.45. Each has a rubber-padded seat on two bolted steel legs with a footrest bar, scuffed grime edges and a stencilled tag.
TABLE TOPS: three or four trays (steel rectangles with divider ridges) holding rations: rationOlive blocks, enamel pellets, a bread roll. Enamel mugs and cupBlue cups with handles, a coffee flask (steel cylinder with an amber band), a salt shaker and a pepper shaker, a few steel cutlery sticks, a crumpled foil pack, an open ration can with a jagged lid ring, and a handheld datapad with a crtGreen screen (glowing) and a mug stain.
Colours: steel, steelDark, steelBright, rubber, enamel, cupBlue, rationOlive, grime, crtGreen, amber.
Keep everything below y 1.1 so hanging lamps overhead clear it.
parts.attaches: Pedestal and bench legs stand on floorTop (y 0.1). Table top at tableTop (y 0.78, centre x 0, z 0.6). Bench tops at benchLeftTop and benchRightTop (y 0.45). Lamps from the overhead part hang above at x 0.

parts.builds:
The right-wall (-X) storage and drinks wall, x -1.7 to -1.1, z -1.95 to 1.35, y 0.1 to 2.1.
LOCKER BANK, z -1.95 to 0.3: three tall locker doors, each about 0.75 m wide and y 0.15 to 2.1, in wallGrey and steelDark with seam, rivets and corner scuffs. One is a FRIDGE (enamel door, thick rubber gasket frame, steel handle, amber temperature readout), one a FREEZER (frosty pale panel with a hazard stripe and heavy latch with red lock light), one a DRY STORE (with a vent louvre grille and padlock). Each has a stencilled label plate, ghost fingerprints (small grime smears) and a kick plate.
COFFEE BENCH, z 0.3 to 1.35: a steel counter top at y 0.95 and cabinets below with two doors and a drawer, plus a toe kick. A big chunky COFFEE MACHINE (steel body, rubber drip tray, glass pot with dark coffee, two dials, an amber ready light, a dispenser nozzle and cup stack). A toaster-like ration heater with an amber glowing slot. A paper cup dispenser tube.
ABOVE THE BENCH: a CRT monitor (rounded box on a bracket) at y 1.3 to 1.85, with a crtGreen menu or readout screen that glows (several thin text-line bars and a header block, a blinking cursor block) and a keypad with amber buttons. A steel shelf above it at y 1.95 holds jars and tins (rationOlive, rust, enamel). A pull-down fold cabinet of emergency rations with a red cross-stripe sign.
Colours: wallGrey, wallDark, steel, steelDark, steelBright, enamel, rubber, hazardYellow, hazardBlack, alarmRed, amber, crtGreen, rationOlive, grime.
Nothing above y 2.1 and nothing protruding past x -1.1.
parts.attaches: Back sits against rightWallFace (x -1.7). Stands on floorTop. Front plane x -1.1 (lockerFront). Bench top at coffeeBenchTop (y 0.95).

parts.builds:
Everything mounted on the back wall (z -2.0 inner face), depth from z -2.0 to -1.75, x ±1.0 only.
HATCH: a heavy blast door at x ±0.55, y 0.1 to 2.0, in a thick steelDark frame with seam and rivet ring. The door leaf is wallGrey with a central wheel lock (a spoked disc: rim torus-like ring of boxes, 6 spokes and hub), vertical stiffener ribs, hinge barrels on the left, and a small porthole with a dark glass disc and a glowing amber ring. Hazard yellow/black chevron strips run on both sides of the frame and across the threshold. A stencilled 'GALLEY' plate and a door number, built as small raised bars, plus a red alarm lamp (alarmRed, glowing) above the frame.
CONTROL PANEL: right of the hatch at x -1.0 to -0.65, y 1.1 to 1.9: a slanted dark console with rows of amber and crtGreen push buttons, 3 toggles, two dials, a small CRT with a crtGreen line (glowing) and an alarmRed push, plus a label strip.
LEFT OF THE HATCH x 0.65 to 1.0: a wall fire-extinguisher (alarmRed cylinder with a black hose and bracket), a first-aid box (enamel with a red cross) and a clipboard of 'duty roster' hanging on a nail.
CONDUIT: vertical pipes (pipeOrange and pipeGrey, with collars and brackets) rise from the floor beside the hatch to the ceiling, and a bundle of black cables runs in a clip rail. A steam vent grille with louvres sits near the ceiling, at x 0 to 0.8, y 2.15 to 2.4. Grime streaks stain below.
Colours: steelDark, wallGrey, wallDark, hazardYellow, hazardBlack, alarmRed, amber, crtGreen, pipeOrange, pipeGrey, rubber, enamel, seam.
parts.attaches: Flush on backWallFace (z -2.0). Hatch centred on hatchCentre (0, 1.05, -2.0). Floor strip at floorTop. Pipes run up to ceilingUnderside (y 2.5), where the overhead part's pipe run starts at z -1.9.

parts.builds:
The ceiling dressing, x ±1.0, y 1.75 to 2.5, hung from the shell's beams at y 2.5.
PIPE RUN: three parallel pipes along z from -1.9 to 2.0 at y about 2.38, in pipeOrange, pipeGrey and a thin black cable tray, with flanged joints every 0.5 m, bolted brackets up to the beams, a valve wheel and a gauge (dial with amber needle), a few drip stains and grime. Elbows turn down at the back end (z -1.9) to meet the back-wall conduit. A rectangular steelDark air duct, x -0.3 to 0.3, y 2.2 to 2.45, runs along z with seam rivets and a louvred outlet face at its front end.
HANGING LAMPS over the table: two caged work lamps at lampMountA (0, 2.5, 0.1) and lampMountB (0, 2.5, 1.1). Each has a short chain or rod down, a steel cage (ring plus 6 bars) and a glowing lampWhite bulb or box, hanging down to y 1.8. One has a spare, slightly crooked cable loop. A ceiling light strip (lampWhite, glowing) between two steel brackets sits near z -1.0.
SMALL EXTRAS: a ceiling speaker horn, an alarmRed beacon with a cage (glowing), a rust patch of steam stain, a tangle of dangling cable ends with taped yellow bands, and a stencilled 'NO SMOKING' plate hanging by chains.
Colours: pipeOrange, pipeGrey, steelDark, steel, rubber, lampWhite, amber, alarmRed, hazardYellow, grime.
All hangs from y 2.5. Lowest point is y 1.75, above the table clutter (below y 1.1).
parts.attaches: Hangs from the beams at ceilingUnderside (y 2.5). Lamps at lampMountA and lampMountB. Pipe run on ceilingPipeRun (y 2.38), reaching the back-wall conduit at z -1.9.

calls.reasoning:
I'm envisioning the Nostromo-style galley: a grungy industrial mess hall with a central table, overhead lamps, ceiling pipes, riveted panels, amber warning lights, CRT screens, and worn stainless steel surfaces.

Now I'm planning the layout and parts breakdown: floor deck, back and side walls, a ceiling frame with hanging pipes for the lamps, open front for a diorama feel, and splitting the build into separate components like the shell structure and counter runs with stainless surfaces, keeping joints minimal since props don't need rigging.

Splitting into shell (floor, walls, ceiling frame) versus services (pipes, vents, hatch, lamps, signage, cabling). I'm working out wall placement and thicknesses so the counter sits flush against the inner face, with the whole room centered on x=0 and spanning roughly 3.6 wide by 4.2 long.

Now I'm building out a tight color palette capped at 24 swatches—worn metal and deck tones, hazard yellow/black striping, grime and rust accents, plus glowing amber, green CRT, and red/cyan light colors for instrument panels.

Then I'm planning the mount points for various scene elements—floor, walls, ceiling underside, counter, table, and lamp positions—to anchor props consistently around the cramped set.

I'm now working out counter and cabinet dimensions along the walls: counter depth and height, overhead cabinets, and leaving the front section open for the doorway. On the right side I'm laying out a run of tall lockers (fridge, freezer, dry store) ending in a coffee/dispenser bench.

I'm splitting the right side into three locker doors plus a wall bench with a coffee machine topped by a monitor and shelf. For the back wall, I'm placing a centered hatch door with hazard stripes, making sure the counters and lockers stay clear of it, and reserving the back wall for hatch, panel, pipe runs, vents, and ceiling lamps.

Now working out the mess table area: table centered small, benches on either side with stools at the ends to keep the aisle clear against the counter front, settling on bench dimensions around 0.28 wide running along z from 0 to 1.2.

I'm tallying part budgets: shell, galley counter, mess table, locker wall, and services sum to 880 out of a 900 cap, with no extra joints needed. I'm noting conventions for builders—floor:true means a part's base sits at y=0, while other parts rest above the floor plane at y=0.1, like the table pedestal which starts there without needing the floor flag.

Now I'm detailing the shell construction itself: a grated deck with slat patterns and hazard striping at the door, beige paneled walls with seams, rivets, and a darker grimy dado near the bottom, corner ribs, and an open ceiling made of a perimeter and cross beam grid rather than a solid surface, with the front side left open and end posts marking the walls.

With the shell box defined, I'm now placing the kitchen counter unit, packing it with cabinets, a steel countertop, a four-burner cooktop with a pot and pan, a glowing oven window, sink, extractor hood, overhead cabinets, a utensil rail, dish rack, and small indicator lights, all kept under the height limit. Next I'm positioning a lockers unit along the opposite wall.

Now I'm working out clearance zones so ceiling pipes, lamps, and service runs along the back wall don't collide with the cabinet tops or locker heights, checking x and y ranges carefully to keep everything above the furniture but below the ceiling.

I'll split into an overheadServices part and a backWall part, adjusting heights so lockers top out at 2.1 and overhead elements start just above that. For hanging lamps over the table, I'm narrowing the overhead box to a central x-range with a lower y-start around 1.75 so they can hang down appropriately without colliding with the side counters.

Simplifying the layout, I'll keep all overhead elements within x±1.0 and treat side conduits as part of the shell beams instead. For budgets, I'm allocating roughly 130 to shell, 170 to counter, 130 to table, 170 to lockers, 140 to backWall, and 140 to overhead, totaling 880, then I'll write out the JSON structure compactly but with enough detail.
